dedupe_keys.name: modelled health facility catchment areas for malawi accessmod travel time catchments

description: This layer divides Malawi into catchment areas, each containing the places for which one health facility is the quickest to reach on foot. The producer is Patrick Kalonde of Youth for Environmental Development, who used the World Health Organization's AccessMod software: its accessibility module merged the road network with land cover, assigned walking speeds, and a least-cost algorithm found the travel time from every location to the nearest facility. Coverage is national, with no travel time cut-off, so even remote communities far from any facility are assigned to one. The polygons are available as a free shapefile download from Zenodo, with a Quarto document describing the method, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: walking only, the facility list and land cover date are not stated in the deposit, travel speeds are assumed, and catchments ignore facility capacity and people choosing a farther facility. Simulation uses: estimating the population served by each facility, testing how closing a facility or losing a river crossing in a flood shifts people to other facilities, and allocating supplies or staff. Related records: the Malawi health facilities layer (data-malawi-health-facilities-registry-dhis2) gives facility points, and AccessMod (model-accessmod) is the software used.
name: Modelled health facility catchment areas for Malawi (AccessMod travel-time catchments)
schema_summary: Polygon layer of catchment areas, each the set of locations whose least-cost walking travel time leads to the same health facility; Quarto file describing the method
